name: Albrechtsburg
_about: THE ALBRECHTSBURG with MEISSEN CATHEDRAL on the Burgberg over the Elbe (x east, z south, from OSM). The castle (1471-1524, Arnold von Westfalen): walls on its real hook-shaped plan, a low ground floor and two high main floors of CURTAIN-ARCH windows, steep tiled roofs, the ring of LUCARNES on the eave (`lucarne`), the Elbe front's tower, and on the court the GROSSER WENDELSTEIN, the open stair tower whose windows climb with its stair (`wendelstein`), and a smaller one. The cathedral: the seven-bay hall nave, the short transept, the long choir, the Hoeckriger Turm, the west towers with their 1903-09 octagons and openwork spires to 81 m, the Fuerstenkapelle; all on the plateau over the rock and its terrace walls.

grosser wendelstein._about: the GROSSER WENDELSTEIN: the open stair tower at the corner of the projection on the court -- the open arcade at its foot, three storeys of great pointed arches over balustrade bands, the loggia, gables and pinnacles round the slate needle

small wendelstein._about: the small stair tower on the court, in the corner of the west wing and the Elbe wing: the same tower, narrower

cathedral nave._about: the seven-bay HALL nave (c. 1410): nave and aisles vaulted at one height on slender piers, tall traceried windows between buttresses, one steep roof over all

cathedral transept._about: the transept, its arms short, a great window in each end

cathedral transept roof._about: the transept's roof, its ridge across the nave's

cathedral choir._about: the long choir (1250-1270), one vessel of tall traceried windows, closed in three sides

cathedral choir roof._about: the choir's roof, hipped round its polygon

cathedral choir buttresses._about: the choir's buttresses down its straight flanks

hoeckriger turm._about: the Hoeckriger Turm, the cathedral's one spire for centuries: its square shaft...

hoeckriger turm octagon._about: ...its octagon, a lancet in every face...

north tower._about: the north west tower: its three square stages (the third Arnold von Westfalen's), to 46 m

south tower._about: the south west tower: its three square stages (the third Arnold von Westfalen's), to 46 m

west tower octagons._about: the octagon on each tower (1903-09), a tall open lancet in every face

west spires._about: the stone spires (1903-09), crocketed ribs on their edges, a gable on every face and pinnacles round their feet: 81 m

west tower pinnacles._about: a pinnacle on each corner of the square towers' heads

west front._about: the west front between the towers, two great windows over each other

west gable._about: the west gable between the octagons

fuerstenkapelle._about: the Fuerstenkapelle, the princes' chapel before the west front, its polygonal end with the portal (now the cathedral's door) and a rose over it

fuerstenkapelle roof._about: its roof, hipped round the polygon

burgberg._about: the Burgberg, the rock spur falling to the Elbe and the Triebisch: battered out wide under the walls

upper rock._about: the rock higher under the town's and the cathedral's sides, the walls there lower

terrace walls._about: the walls round the plateau's edge, rubble on the rock; the plateau over them

burg stair._about: the way up: a flight along the west terrace wall's foot to the Domplatz

burg stair forecourt._about: the masonry forecourt on the rock at the stair's foot
